decisive_spans.text: areas of fat attenuation located in the upper pole
creating a defect in the renal parenchyma. The lesion contained visible vessels extending into the renal cortex, a finding known as a “renal parenchymal vascular pedicle.”
a fatty tumor thrombus within the right renal vein extending to its confluence with the inferior vena cava

response.rationale: The presence of a renal mass with fat attenuation, visible vessels extending into the renal cortex (renal parenchymal vascular pedicle), and a fatty tumor thrombus in the renal vein strongly supports Angiomyolipoma. While other renal cell carcinomas can have tumor thrombus, the 'fatty' nature of the thrombus and the fat attenuation in the mass are key features of Angiomyolipoma. Renal cell carcinoma with tumor thrombus (D4) is a runner-up due to the tumor thrombus, but lacks the specific 'fatty' description of the mass and thrombus.
